title: Depth-Recurrent Attention Mixture (Dreamer): Giving Latent Reasoning the Attention it Deserves
claim: One recurring layer composes attention over depth, sequence and experts, so a single shared block gains reasoning capacity and scaling flexibility.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; sequence-by-depth grid zooms into three color-coded attention modules
description: The left panel is a grid of recurrent layer nodes (θ). Sequence positions 1…t run along the x-axis and depth 1…l runs up the y-axis. Faded earlier nodes feed the highlighted node at position t and depth l. Teal arrows show sequence attention (SA) from earlier tokens. Gold arrows show depth attention (DA) from lower depths. Red-pink arrows show expert attention (EA) from a column of sparse expert slots. A dotted zoom cone leads to the right panel. The right panel has three colored boxes in sequence: Depth Attention (gold), Sequence Attention (teal) and Expert Attention (red). Each box shows linear projections, RoPE icons and Q/K/V flows into a sparse attention block. A residual line with ⊕ nodes runs from x_{t,l} to x_{t,l+1}. A legend along the bottom defines the icons.
caption: Depth-recurrent attention mixture (Dreamer). This instance combines attention over sequence (horizontal), depth (vertical), and sparse experts (right) in a single recurring layer, to facilitate knowledge reuse, alleviate hidden- and layer-size bottlenecks, improve reasoning and data efficiency, and decouple scaling dimensions (params, FLOPs, depth, and depth-wise memory).
abstract: Depth-recurrence facilitates latent reasoning by sharing parameters across depths. However, prior work lacks combined FLOP-, parameter-, and memory-matched baselines, underutilizes depth-recurrence due to partially fixed layer stacks, and ignores the bottleneck of constant hidden-sizes that restricts many-step latent reasoning. To address this, we introduce a modular framework of depth-recurrent attention mixtures (Dreamer), combining sequence attention, depth attention, and sparse expert attention. It alleviates the hidden-size bottleneck through attention along depth, decouples scaling dimensions, and allows depth-recurrent models to scale efficiently and effectively. Across language reasoning benchmarks, our models require 2 to 8x fewer training tokens for the same accuracy as FLOP-, parameter-, and memory-matched SOTA, and outperform ca. 2x larger SOTA models with the same training tokens. We further present insights into knowledge usage across depths, e.g., showing 2 to 11x larger expert selection diversity than SOTA MoEs.
